source: Mortgage News Daily, Freddie Mac, Zillow and HousingWire

headline: Rates hit 7.5%
*in three days*
slides.fig_caption: percentage points on the daily 30-year index, Nov. 9 to Nov. 13
slides.sub: A hotter-than-expected inflation report pushed the 30-year from 7.18% to 7.50%.

slides.label: *Fourth straight drop* in Freddie Mac's weekly average
slides.body: The weekly survey mostly reflects the calm days before the Nov. 10 inflation report. Daily quotes ran higher: the Mortgage News Daily index closed the week at 7.50%.

slides.title: A one-week *rate jump*
slides.note: The 5/1 ARM average, *7.45%*, now sits above the 30-year fixed average of 7.27%.

slides.title: What moved, *and why*
points: *0.4% vs. 0.3%:* October consumer prices beat forecasts; core rose 0.3% vs. 0.2%.
*5.10%:* the 10-year Treasury yield on Nov. 12, up from 4.86% on Nov. 6.
*+8%:* purchase applications week over week, per HousingWire's tracker.
*About $67 a month:* added principal and interest on a $300,000 loan at 7.50% vs. 7.17%.

slides.title: Rerun the *payment math*
slides.body: Weekly averages lag fast moves. Have buyers refresh preapprovals and confirm today's quote with their lender before writing offers, so a sudden jump doesn't surprise anyone at the table.
